description: This line plot illustrates the training loss for six different model architectures—ChemBART Small 20M (red), ChemBART Medium 20M (blue), ChemBERTa Small 20M (green), ChemBERTa Medium 20M (orange), ChemLLaMA Small 20M (purple), and ChemLLaMA Medium 20M (brown)—as a function of training step, all trained on a dataset of 20 million samples. The x-axis, labeled "Step," is linearly scaled from 0 to 440,000 steps, with major gridlines and tick labels at intervals of 20,000 steps (0K, 20K, 40K, 60K, 80K, 420K, 430K, 440K). The y-axis, labeled "Train Loss," is linearly scaled from 0.0 to 0.85. All lines begin at a high training loss near 0.8, rapidly decreasing in the initial steps, and then converge toward a stable, low-loss plateau. The ChemBERTa Small 20M model (green) exhibits the steepest initial decline, reaching approximately 0.15 at 440,000 steps. The ChemLLaMA Medium 20M model (brown) consistently achieves the lowest loss among all models, stabilizing near 0.01 at 440,000 steps. The ChemBART Small 20M model (red) shows a slower rate of decline compared to ChemLLaMA Small 20M (purple), stabilizing at approximately 0.25 at 440,000 steps. The ChemLLaMA Medium 20M model (brown) consistently outperforms ChemBART Medium 20M (blue) throughout the training process.
caption_used: Training Loss vs. Steps for Each Model Type by Model Size with a Data Size of 20 million. The loss trends for 10 million and 20 million datasets are similar. The ChemBERTa Small 20M model exhibits the steepest decline in training loss, reaching approximately 0.15 at 440k steps. ChemLLaMA Medium 20M consistently outperforms ChemBART Medium 20M, achieving the lowest loss of all models at 0.01. The ChemBART Small 20M model shows a slower rate of decline compared to ChemLLaMA Small 20M, stabilizing at around 0.25 at 440k steps.
